mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the FEDFUNDS rate above the 5-year moving average precedes a short-term decline in S&P 500 20-day forward returns due to tightened discount rates affecting future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its 5-period SMA by at least 0.2 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 5-period mean during the trigger period, or FEDFUNDS does not exceed the SMA by the required threshold.

mechanism_narrative: Rising monthly employment (PAYEMS) accompanied by falling unemployment (UNRATE) signals a strong labor market, which is associated with positive S&P 500 60-day forward returns via optimism about growth.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% while UNRATE falls by at least 0.5 percentage points over the next month
failure_condition: Over a 60-day window, SPX 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during a comparable period of weak labor indicators (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden surge in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month high coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as it signals expanding economic demand for capital goods.
failure_condition: 12-month high in INDPRO is not followed by a statistically significant positive 20-day forward return (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive decline in consumer inflation (CPIAUCSL) below 2% for three consecutive months predicts a 20-day S&P 500 forward return decline as market anticipates lower rate hike risk.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls below 2.0 for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall as predicted during the three-month CPIAUCSL < 2.0 period.

mechanism_narrative: When FEDFUNDS remains below 2% for two consecutive months, the S&P 5-day forward return is positive as markets anticipate accommodative policy sustaining equity valuations.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive during the two-month FEDFUNDS < 2% window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp drop in job openings (HOUST) accompanied by a rise in unemployment (UNRATE) indicates softening labor markets, which is associated with negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns due to risk aversion.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls by at least 10% while UNRATE increases by at least 0.3 percentage points over the next quarter
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns do not show the expected negative deviation during the defined labor market transition.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive monthly declines in industrial production (INDPRO) for three months predict a regime where S&P 20-day forward returns turn negative due to supply-side weakness.
failure_condition: During the three-month INDPRO decline, 20-day forward returns do not trend lower than the prior three-month average.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) above 3% triggers a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return as markets anticipate aggressive rate hikes that depress equity valuations.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3.0 by at least 0.5 percentage points
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive or flat during the inflation spike period.
